items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-04-04
items.q: Oh, yeah. I made a record with him.

ctx.x: That's what I'm telling you now, all that come to them. There wasn't at the beginning. Yeah. But all that come to them, man. Everything. It really come to them. Like Winging Alone and Primo. Boy, them boys would start out playing us a straight home, but they got together, they got all that stuff together like everybody else, you know.
Oh, I wanted to ask you about Frankie Halfpaint Jackson. You made a record with him, huh? Oh, yeah. I made a record with him. You remember who was in that band?

Yeah, Francois Mosley's band. Charlie Ducasse, myself, Fred Reed on piano. And Charlie Ducasse on guitar and that boy, Lil Sax on tenor. Fred Howard on alto. He played alto on clarinet. And what else? Fred on piano, me on trumpet. Al Wynn on trombone. Al Wynn. I got a letter from him the other day. Little Sax's name is what? Robert Crowder. Everybody called him. You know who he was, Kenta? Y'all didn't know Cecil. He used to play with Earl Hein.

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1957-multiple
items.q: We thought maybe it was Frankie Halfbine with the vocal

ctx.x: I thought that record came out on their, under another name, too. Yeah.

Like one of the Jimmy Blythe groups. Yeah, I think maybe it did. Uh, Cathedral Blues he's on, and Dixieland Doings the other side, it's another trouble. We thought maybe it was Frankie Halfbine with the vocal, but he can't hear too well.

Uh, do you know anything about Tiny Parham? I never did get to talk to him. I saw him play once at the Savoy Ballroom in 1938. Yeah. He's a big, big, fat doll was playing the organ. That's right. And I went over there with Mead Lux Lewis, and I said, who's the organist? He said, oh, everybody knows him. If you know him, that's Tiny. Yeah, that's right. A big, big, big fella.
